questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: What property defines a binary min-heap?
options: Every parent key is no greater than either child key
Every array position is globally sorted in ascending order
Every leaf key is smaller than every internal-node key
Every left child is smaller than its corresponding right child

questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: In a zero-based heap array, what is the left-child index of node i?
options: i divided by 2

questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: After appending a new min-heap key, which operation restores heap order?
options: Scan every leaf and globally sort the complete array
Replace the root and discard the new final array slot
Sift the new key upward while it is smaller than its parent
Move the new key downward while it is smaller than either child

questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: How does extract-min avoid shifting every remaining array element?
options: It leaves the removed root in place and changes only the size counter
It swaps every pair of siblings before returning the final leaf
It binary-searches for a duplicate minimum and removes that duplicate
It moves the final element to the root, shrinks, and sifts downward

questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: Why does bottom-up heapify run in O(n) rather than O(n log n)?
options: Most nodes are near leaves and can sift only a small distance
Every internal node is already guaranteed to satisfy heap order
Heapify examines only the root and ignores all descendant keys
A complete tree has constant height regardless of its node count

questions.topic: Binary Heap Mechanics: Insert and Extract-Min
questions.question: Why is arbitrary-key search still O(n) in a min-heap?
options: The heap uses linked nodes and therefore lacks array indexes
Ancestor order does not identify which branch contains an arbitrary key
Every lookup must first remove all keys smaller than the requested key
The minimum is stored at an unknown leaf rather than at the root

questions.topic: Maintaining Top-k with a Bounded Min-Heap
questions.question: Why does a top-k-largest algorithm use a min-heap?
options: The root stores the strongest winner for immediate output
The root stores the smallest loser seen anywhere in the stream
The root exposes the weakest retained winner as the admission threshold
A min-heap automatically stores all candidates in descending order

questions.topic: Maintaining Top-k with a Bounded Min-Heap
questions.question: What happens when a new score does not exceed the root of a full top-k min-heap?
options: The root is removed and the new lower score is inserted
The entire heap is sorted before making the decision
The heap doubles its capacity to retain the additional candidate
The candidate is discarded because it cannot enter the winners

questions.topic: Maintaining Top-k with a Bounded Min-Heap
questions.question: What are the standard worst-case time and retained-space bounds for bounded-heap top-k over n scores?
options: O(n log n) time and O(n) space
O(n log k) time and O(k) space
O(k log n) time and O(1) space
O(log k) time and O(nk) space

questions.topic: Maintaining Top-k with a Bounded Min-Heap
questions.question: Why should equal scores use a stable secondary key?
options: It raises every equal score above the current admission threshold
It reduces the heap height from logarithmic to constant
It makes survivor selection reproducible across traversal and shard timing
It lets the heap retain more than k candidates without resizing

questions.topic: Maintaining Top-k with a Bounded Min-Heap
questions.question: When might each shard need to return more than its local top k?
options: When the coordinator uses the identical pure score order
When every shard contains fewer than k total documents
When document scores and tie-breaking are globally deterministic
When a later objective adds diversity, quotas, or different reranking

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: What unnecessary work does full sorting perform for a small top-k request?
options: It establishes relative order among losers that the consumer never receives
It retains only k records and discards all other scores immediately
It avoids comparing candidates that cannot beat the current threshold
It processes the input as a stream without materializing scored records

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: Does a bounded heap directly return its k winners in descending score order?
options: Yes, because every heap array is globally descending
No, the final k winners still require sorting for ranked output
Yes, because the minimum root is also the strongest winner
No, because a heap cannot identify which candidates are winners

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: For n = 1,000,000 and k = 10, which comparison-scale estimate matches heap top-k?
options: Roughly 1,000,000 squared comparison units
Roughly 20 million comparison units from n log2 n
Roughly 3.3 million comparison units from n log2 k
Roughly ten comparison units because only winners are inspected

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: Which workload most strongly favors a bounded heap over quickselect?
options: A small mutable array that is already fully resident in memory
A request to output every scored item in complete order
A batch where retaining the full input has no memory cost
A stream larger than memory that needs only 100 winners

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: When does the asymptotic selection advantage of heap top-k disappear?
options: When k approaches n, so log k approaches log n
When k equals one, so only one admission threshold exists
When candidates arrive as a stream rather than a batch
When final winners use deterministic secondary keys

questions.topic: Heap-Based Top-k vs Full Sort: Cost Comparison
questions.question: A product must export every record sorted by score. Which choice is appropriate?
options: Keep a size-10 heap because losers never require ordering
Perform a full in-memory or external sort because complete order is required
Use quickselect once and leave both partitions internally unordered
Discard records below the first observed score to reduce output work
